messages.content: i put two apples in a basket and left it by the kitchen door. then my father carried the basket to the table.
the basket is on the table now, with the two apples inside.
he took one apple out and put it on a plate. where are the apples?
one apple is on the plate, and one is still in the basket.
i moved the plate to the shelf. did i move the basket too?
no. you only said you moved the plate. the basket is still on the table.
which apple is on the shelf?
the apple your father put on the plate.
write a little about a quiet morning at home. use i.
i open the window and let the morning air into the room. then i make tea and sit by the table. my book is open, but i take a little time to look outside before i start reading.
now make it about yesterday.
yesterday, i opened the window and let the morning air into the room. then i made tea and sat by the table. my book was open, but i took a little time to look outside before i started reading.
did you change what the person did?
no. i kept the same things and changed the time to yesterday.
my friend is tired but i would like to see her. what can i say?
you could ask if she would like a short visit and let her know it is okay to rest instead.
write it for me. do not make her feel she has to come.
i would like to see you, but i know you are tired. would you like a short visit, or would you like to rest at home today? we can meet another time.
i would be the one going to her house.
i would like to visit you, but i know you are tired. would a short visit be okay, or would you like to rest today? we can meet another time.
write a talk where a student does not hear a question at school.

teacher: what did the girl bring to the park? student: sorry, i did not hear the question. could you say it again, please? teacher: yes. what did the girl bring to the park? student: she brought her book. teacher: that is right. student: thank you for saying it again.
did the teacher give the student the answer?
no. the teacher said the question again, and the student gave the answer.
make the thing the student asks shorter.
could you say that again, please?
i am hungry, but i do not want soup. does that mean i do not want to eat?
no. you can be hungry and still not want soup. you may want another kind of food.
i would like bread and an egg.
then you could have bread and an egg instead of soup.
my friend says i should just eat the soup because it is there.
you can say: thank you, but i do not feel like soup. i would like bread and an egg instead.
keep only the thing i should say.
thank you, but i do not feel like soup. i would like bread and an egg instead.
i want the book with the story about the boy and the boat. my sister says it is blue.
you are looking for the story about the boy and the boat. the blue color may help you find it.
i found a blue book, but it is about a girl at school.
then it is not the story you asked for. the color alone does not make it the right book.
should i ask my sister again?
yes. you could say: this blue book is about a girl at school. where is the one about the boy and the boat?
write a short letter to my father about learning to ride a bike. do not say i can do it alone now.

hello, father. i tried riding a bike today. my friend helped me, and i learned a little more than last time. i still need help, but i am happy i tried again. i would like to show you when you visit. love, your child.
can you make it from a daughter?

hello, father. i tried riding a bike today. my friend helped me, and i learned a little more than last time. i still need help, but i am happy i tried again. i would like to show you when you visit. love, your daughter.
i do not need help with work. i just want to talk for a little while.
okay. we can just talk. how has your day been?
quiet. i cleaned the kitchen and sat outside for a while.
a little time outside can be nice. did you enjoy sitting there?
yes. i watched a bird near the wall.
a little time watching a bird can be a nice part of a quiet day.
please do not ask me to turn it into a story or a plan.
okay. we can leave it as a nice little part of your day.
help me write about my village. it has a school, a shop, and a little street.
there is a school and a shop in my village. there is a little street too.
there is another street too. make it about both.
my village has a school and a shop. one little street goes by the school, and another goes by the shop.
the school and shop are on the same street.
my village has a school and a shop on one little street. there is another little street too.
i would like my friend to read a book i love, but she is busy.
you could ask if she would like to read the book when she has time.
write it as a short note.
i love this book and think you may enjoy it too. you are welcome to read it when you have time. you do not have to start now.
i do not know if she will enjoy it. just ask if she would like to read it.
i love this book. would you like to read it when you have time? it is okay if you do not want to.
i said i would wash the cups before reading. now i want to read first.
you can change the order if the cups do not need to be ready right away. read for a while, then wash them.
my mother will need them for tea after lunch.
then wash the cups first so they are ready for tea. you can read after that.
i am not sure if she will have tea right after lunch or later in the afternoon.
then washing the cups before lunch will have them ready for both. you can read after you wash them.
in my picture a boy is standing behind a chair. a girl is sitting on the chair.
the girl is on the chair, and the boy is behind it.
the girl stands up and moves to the window. who is on the chair now?
no one is on the chair now, from what you said.
could the boy be sitting there?
he could sit there next, but you have not said he did. the last thing you said about him was that he was standing behind the chair.
yes, he is still standing there.
then the chair has no one sitting on it.
i had a good day, so why do i feel tired?
you can have a good day and still do much that makes you tired. being happy about your day does not mean you will not need rest.
so being tired does not mean the day was wrong?
right. you can feel happy about the day and still need rest.
i walked with my family and helped cook dinner.
you walked and helped with dinner. that can make you tired even if you enjoy it. you may want a quiet rest now.
my friend said sorry for not answering my note. i did not mind. what can i say?
no problem. i know you have been busy. it is nice to hear from you.
i do not know if she was busy.
no problem. it is nice to hear from you. how have you been?
do not add a question.
no problem. it is nice to hear from you.
does that sound cold?
it is short, but still kind. you can add: i am happy we can talk again.
tell me a little story about a girl looking for her lost pen. she does not find it in the story.

a girl opened her bag to get her pen, but it was not there. she looked under her book and inside a small box on her desk. the pen was not in the box. she asked her brother if he had it. he said no, but he could help her look after lunch. the girl put her book back in the bag and chose a pencil for now. she still did not know where the pen was, but she could finish her writing while she waited for her brother.
did she find the pen?
no. she chose a pencil so she could write while she waited.
what does before lunch mean?
lunch comes after the thing you are talking about. for example, you could read in the morning before having lunch.
can you make that shorter?
the thing comes first. lunch comes after it.
give me a sentence about washing my hands.
i wash my hands before lunch.
and after lunch?
i wash my hands after lunch. in that sentence, lunch comes first, and you wash your hands after it.
i want to talk about books, but not about school.
okay. we can talk about books you choose to read at home. what kind do you like?
quiet books about people at home.
you may enjoy a story about small things in a family, where we learn how the people feel.
i do not need a list of books. just talk with me about why i like that.
maybe the quiet things feel close to your own life, or you enjoy getting to know people through what they do each day.
yes, the part about getting to know people.
then you may care more about the people in the story than about a big journey.
i am making tea for my mother. she does not like sugar in it.
then make her tea with no sugar. does she like milk?
yes, a little. i put sugar in my own tea.
make her cup with a little milk and no sugar. then make your own cup with sugar.
so i do not put sugar in both?
right. only put sugar in your own cup.
which cup has sugar?
your cup has sugar. the cup for your mother does not.
tell my uncle i can visit tomorrow afternoon but have to leave before dinner.
i can visit tomorrow afternoon, but i will have to leave before dinner.
ask if that is okay with him.
i can visit tomorrow afternoon, but i will have to leave before dinner. would that be okay with you?
i am going to say it on the phone. make it easy to say.
can i come over tomorrow afternoon? i need to leave before dinner.
does that still ask if it is okay?
yes. can i come over asks if he is okay with the visit.
i like tea, a quiet room, and reading by the window. what do you know about me?
you said you like tea, a quiet room, and reading by the window.
does that mean i never like being with people?
no. you did not say that. you can like quiet time and still enjoy being with people.
what if i say i also love dinner with my family?
then i know you said you enjoy quiet time and dinner with your family. both can be true.
write a short talk where two children want the same pencil.

girl: can i use that pencil? boy: i am writing with it now. girl: can i have it when you finish? boy: yes. i just need to finish this line. girl: okay. i will get my paper ready while i wait. boy: i am done now. here you are. girl: thank you. boy: you are welcome.
did the girl take it while he was writing?
no. she waited for him to finish.
what did she do while waiting?
she got her paper ready.
what color is the hat in my picture?
i cannot tell from what you have said. what does the hat look like?
it is red with a black line around it.
then the hat is red with a black line, from what you said.
did you look at it?
no. i answered from what you said about it.
say the color again, just one word.
red.
give me a sentence about a bird, then a question about the same bird.
a little bird sits on the wall. what color is the bird?
now give the answer too. make it brown.
a little bird sits on the wall. what color is the bird? the bird is brown.
make the bird sit in a tree instead.
a little bird sits in a tree. what color is the bird? the bird is brown.
did you change its color?
no. i changed where it sits. it is still brown.
my brother calls while i am cooking. i want to talk but cannot listen well then.
you could say you would like to talk after you finish cooking.
write the words for me.
i would like to talk, but i am cooking right now and cannot listen well. can i call you after dinner?
do not choose after dinner. i will be free before that.
i would like to talk, but i am cooking right now and cannot listen well. can i call you when i finish cooking?
write a little about an open window. make it calm and short.

the window is open, and the air in the room feels nice. a book is on the table next to a cup of tea. outside, a bird moves from the wall to the tree. the person by the window can stay home for a while. there is time to sit, read, and listen.
make it about me. use i.

my window is open, and the air in the room feels nice. my book is on the table next to my cup of tea. outside, a bird moves from the wall to the tree. i can stay home for a while. there is time to sit, read, and listen.
should i bring a coat for my walk? it is warm outside.
if it is still warm later and you will not be out long, you may not need one.
i will be out all evening, and it may get cold.
then bringing a coat may be a good idea, so you have it if the air gets cold.
why did your answer change?
you gave me more to think about. first you said it was warm. then you said you would be out all evening and it might get cold.
tell me a story about a family taking lunch to a park. they leave the big pot at home.

a family made lunch in a big pot. when the food was ready, they put some into a small box for their trip. the pot was too big to carry with all their other things, so they left it in the kitchen. at the park, they sat under a tree and opened the box. they had lunch and watched people walking by. after they ate, they put the box back in the bag. then they went home, where the big pot was still in the kitchen.
did they carry the pot to the park?
no. they carried a small box of food and left the pot at home.
how can i ask someone to open a window? give me one short sentence.
could you open the window, please?
now make it about closing the door.
could you close the door, please?
make that about two people, but still one sentence.
could one of you close the door, please?
are you asking both of them to do it together?
no. i am asking one of them to close it.
i am going to visit my aunt. i have been to her house before. can i say i am going back?
yes. going back can mean you are going to a place where you have been before.
what if she moved to a new house and i have never been there?
then say you are going to visit her at her new house. going back to the house would make it sound like you had been there before.
but i have met my aunt before.
yes. you can visit the same person at a new place. the person and the place do not have to be new together.
make this shorter: i have a cup, and i have a plate, and i have a spoon, but i do not have a fork.
i have a cup, a plate, and a spoon, but no fork.
now ask my sister to bring what i do not have.
could you bring a fork, please?
why not ask for a spoon too?
you already said you have a spoon. the fork is the thing you said you do not have.
now i found a fork in the bag.
then you have the fork too, so you do not need to ask her to bring one.
